findings.title: Task 1's fixture plan won't parse and breaks existing tests
findings.description:
There are two separate problems.

1. **The unindexed example line won't match.** The example is `7. [~] Feature Epsilon without explicit index — cut for scope.` and it has no bold markers. `PLAN_UNINDEXED_RE` requires the name in bold (`\*\*([^(].*?)\*\*`, at `packages/core/src/introspection/parsers/slicePlanParser.ts:9`). So even after Task 2 adds `~` to the regex, this line is still silently dropped. The slice design's own criterion uses the bold form: `N. [~] **Name** — rationale`. Task 1's success line makes this worse by asking for the bold wrapper only "for the indexed form". A junior AI following the task exactly would see Task 5 fail. It might then loosen the regex, which is out of scope.

2. **Changing the shared fixture breaks tests the task file doesn't list.** Even with a correctly bolded unindexed line, these existing tests would fail:
   - `packages/core/tests/introspection/ArtifactIntrospector.test.ts:52` checks `totalSlices` is 5. No task updates it.
   - `packages/core/tests/introspection/slicePlanParser.test.ts:126-129` checks every entry in this fixture is `indexSource: 'explicit'`. An unindexed entry breaks that.
   - An unindexed entry gets index `unindexedCounter = 1`. The parser sorts by index (`slicePlanParser.ts:91`), so the new entry moves to `entries[0]`. That breaks the `entries[0]` and `entries[2]` checks at lines 12 and 22 and the description checks at lines 166-167.

   This also contradicts the slice design's last success criterion: regression safety is "proven by the existing `sample-slice-plan.md` fixture tests continuing to pass unchanged."

**Fix:** use the alternative the design already allows ("or add a sibling fixture"). Create a new fixture such as `deprecated-slice-plan.md` holding one indexed and one bolded unindexed `[~]` line, and leave `sample-slice-plan.md` untouched. Then:
- Task 5 no longer edits the existing `totalSlices`/`completedSlices` test.
- Task 5's extra "byte-identical regression test" can be deleted, because the unchanged existing tests already prove there's no regression.

findings.title: Task 8 wrongly claims `resolveEntryStatus` gets a full `SlicePlanEntry`
findings.description: Task 8 says the only caller of `resolveEntryStatus` "passes a full `SlicePlanEntry`". In fact the only caller is `resolveEntryStatusSafe`, and it declares its own parameter as `Pick<SlicePlanEntry, 'index' | 'isChecked'>` (line 736) before passing it on. If only `resolveEntryStatus`'s `Pick` is widened, the build fails. Task 8 should say to add `'status'` to both `Pick` types.

findings.title: Task 9's fallback-initializer step does nothing, and its reasoning is wrong
findings.description:
Task 9 changes the `derivedStatus` initializer at line 91, saying it's the fallback "if `detectDocuments` throws". It isn't. Every path overwrites it:
- the `try` block assigns it at line 122;
- the `catch` block sets it to `'degraded'` at line 126.

So the change has no effect, and its stated goal (report `deprecated` instead of `not-started` on a filesystem error) doesn't happen. Remove the step. The design only asks for one added line in the `deriveEntryStatus({...})` call.

Related NOTE: if a `[~]` entry has an unreadable task file or an unrecognised frontmatter status, it still shows as `degraded` in both `slice.ts` and `resolveEntryStatusSafe`. `findFirstNotCompleteEntry` treats `degraded` as not complete, so that entry could be offered as next. The design doesn't cover this case. Leaving it is acceptable, but it's worth knowing.

findings.title: `arch-status-vs-plans` has no test, though the success criterion names it
findings.description: The success criterion covers both `plan-status-vs-entries` and `arch-status-vs-plans`. Task 12 tests only the first. Both rules use the same `completedSlices === totalSlices` check, so one extra case in Task 12 would cover it: architecture `status: complete`, with a plan whose entries are all `[x]` or `[~]`, and no finding produced.

findings.title: Commit markers are written as checkboxes
findings.description: The commit markers at Tasks 5, 7, 10, 11, 12 and 13 are written as `- [ ] Commit: ...`. They should be plain `**Commit**:` lines, not checklist items. Where they sit is fine. The parser, derivation and wiring commits each fall at a tested point.

findings.title: Task 11 tests Task 8 but comes after the CLI work
findings.description: Task 11 is the test for Task 8's change to `WorkflowNavigator`, but Tasks 9 and 10 (the CLI work) sit between them. Moving Task 11 directly after Task 8 matches the pattern of putting each test right after its code. Task 8 could then commit on its own, and Task 10 would cover only the CLI.

findings.title: The task file is heavier than about ten lines of production code needs
findings.description:
Thirteen tasks and six commits is a lot for this change. Three ways to trim it:
- Merge Tasks 2–4 into one parser task. Each one changes only a line or two in the same function.
- Merge the test-only commits for Tasks 11 and 12.
- The manual walkthrough in Task 13 repeats what the automated tests already check. Running `pnpm -r build` and `pnpm -r test` is enough.
